title: Join the Online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action’ on 7 December 2026
content:
Europa Nostra and the Office of Public Works Ireland (OPW) are hosting the online Masterclass ‘Balancing Heritage Conservation and Climate Action on Monday 7 December 2026 (13:00-14:30 CET / 12:00-13:30 WET).

This masterclass explores the methodology, practical experience and key outcomes of the initiative Improving the Energy Performance of Heritage Properties in State Care, which has been developed by OPW to support the country’s climate action commitments and the EU’s decarbonisation targets. At the time, no clear framework existed for improving the energy performance of historic buildings while safeguarding their heritage value. The initiative offers valuable insights and lessons learned that can be adapted and applied in other contexts and settings. The initiative received both a European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award and the Grand Prix 2026 in the Education, Training and Skills categories.

Register now

This online masterclass is organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, which is supported by the Creative Europe programme of the European Union.

title: Europa Nostra participates in the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters” held in Brussels
content:
Today, Europa Nostra is attending the European Parliament’s event “Invest in What Matters – Debating and Communicating the MFF and National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs)”.

Building on yesterday’s Joint Statement by the Cultural Deal for Europe partners, which calls on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme, we must ensure that culture and heritage are also recognised across the EU’s other funding instruments, particularly the future National and Regional Partnership Plans for 2028–2034.

Photo credit: Europa Nostra

In her opening remarks, European Parliament President Roberta Metsola reminded us that the EU budget has a real impact on people’s lives. She stressed the importance of empowering cities and regions, involving local and regional authorities in designing and implementing the plans, and communicating what EU funding makes possible.

Why does heritage matter? Because the places, traditions and landscapes that shape our identity and sense of belonging also contribute to well-being, social cohesion, jobs, sustainable tourism and more attractive, resilient territories.

title: Joint Statement – Cultural Deal for Europe partners call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to the AgoraEU programme
content:
The Cultural Deal for Europe is a trans-national, cross-sector partnership co-initiated by Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation

Ahead of the EU Economic and Financial Affairs Council of 10 November 2026, which will discuss the EU’s next budget (2028-2034), we, Culture Action Europe, Europa Nostra and the European Cultural Foundation – co-initiators of the Cultural Deal for Europe – call on the EU Council to reject the 30% cut to AgoraEU proposed by the Irish Presidency. Chopping €2.58 billion for culture, media, cultural heritage, and civil society – essential to Europe’s democratic resilience and hence the basis for our better future – would not only cause profound damage to an already heavily impacted culture (both arts and heritage) and media sectors but only save just 0.14% of the EU budget.

title: British-Turkish novelist Elif Shafak receives Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 in Lisbon
content:
“Literature has a very gentle but very profound power and resilience. It gives us hope and continues to connect us beyond all borders of identity, geography and time,” stated Elif Shafak, renowned British-Turkish novelist and storyteller after receiving the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness of Cultural Heritage 2026 at a ceremony held on 5 November at the Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.

High-level representatives of the partners and supporters of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award – namely the President of Centro Nacional de Cultura, Maria Calado, the Secretary General of Europa Nostra, Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović, and the representative of the Gulbenkian Foundation in the Award Jury, Guilherme d’Oliveira Martins – as well as the Mayor of Lisbon, Carlos Moedas, addressed the audience. The ceremony was attended by some 200 people. Among the guests of honour was the former President of Portugal, Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa.
